narrative: A mother in her early forties left her small home town near Damascus in 2011, soon after the government assaults began, taking her two young children and her seven-year-old nephew. She went first to Jordan, where she spent three years in the massive Zaatari refugee camp. She decided to leave after a Jordanian policeman suggested it would be safer if she married her very young daughter off to him. Her journey to Berlin, via Turkey, took three months. She traveled in a group of 250 people but was the only one with children, and she felt others worried she would slow the group down. In Macedonia the police caught her and threatened to send her back to Greece. She was so determined and desperate that she put a knife to her own throat and declared she would rather die than retrace her journey. The police, taken aback, then helped her onward to the Serbian border. In Hungary, a hotel owner took her money and then called the police on her. She arrived in Berlin in May and lived there in a group home.
